title: Sweep VCF Operations for Networks troubleshooting incidents completely and in stable order
prompt: Implement the `Vcf.Operations.Networks` PowerShell module described by the pinned VCF 9.0 contract in `docs/contract.json`. Create its manifest and root module at `Vcf.Operations.Networks/Vcf.Operations.Networks.psd1` and `Vcf.Operations.Networks/Vcf.Operations.Networks.psm1`. The environment provides the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` module version `13.5.0.25380678`; declare it as a required module dependency and do not vendor, redefine, or imitate VMware modules or other third-party binaries. That generated SDK has no cmdlet for the VCF Operations for Networks `/api/ni` surface, so issue the contract request directly over HTTP from PowerShell. Export `Get-VcfOperationsNetworkTroubleshootingIncident` with mandatory `-ServerUri` (`[uri]`) and `-ApiToken` (`[string]`) parameters and optional `-PageSize` (`[double]`) and `-StartEntityId` (`[string]`) parameters. Use only the contract operation `listTroubleshootingIncidents` to retrieve every cursor page, preserving any explicitly supplied collection parameters on every page. Send the API token using the contract's authentication scheme. Do not send optional query fields when their parameters were not supplied. Emit one complete object per incident, after collecting all pages, in ascending ordinal order by `entity_id`. Keep the supplied contract, official-source record, loopback mock, and verifier unchanged. Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1` to verify the implementation; the verifier uses only the loopback service and never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
